relationship.locator: University Physics 1 Eq. 15.1 and section 16.1 periodic-wave definitions
relationship.translation_notes: Serialize source Eq. 15.1 in the inverse direction T=1/f, preserving a single canonical relationship. 1 is the dimensionless count of one complete cycle, not an empirical coefficient. Dimensions 1/T^-1=T. Hz and s both have unit scale in the current registry. The period is elapsed time for exactly one repeat, not any generic event duration.

variables.definition: Positive cycle frequency of the specified periodic wave or oscillator in the given time frame.
variables.context: Same periodic wave, oscillator or repeated phase train, fixed time coordinate and operating conditions; a cycle returns to the same phase, and period is continuous elapsed duration per cycle, not accumulated operating hours.
variables.domain: Finite strictly positive constant cycle frequency.

variables.definition: Continuous elapsed time for exactly one complete repeat of the specified oscillation or phase.
variables.context: Same periodic wave, oscillator or repeated phase train, fixed time coordinate and operating conditions; a cycle returns to the same phase, and period is continuous elapsed duration per cycle, not accumulated operating hours.

assumptions: Source definition: a periodic process repeats after one cycle, with a stable period/frequency in the selected interval and time frame.
limitations: Zero frequency corresponds to no finite repeating cycle and cannot be assigned an infinite scalar period.
Aperiodic signals and a broadband spectrum do not have one such period; a selected periodic component must be specified.
This record is retained solely to correct the prior return's missed catalog overlap; numerical validity does not make it new scientific coverage.

references.method: Published Example 16.1(b) gives 0.50 s, retained as expected. Half its final 0.01 s reporting step gives 0.005 s tolerance; this is an arithmetic example, not measured uncertainty.

Independent synthetic counting: ten complete equally timed cycles span 25 s, so each lasts 25/10=2.5 s, while frequency is ten cycles/25 s=0.4 Hz. Expected is obtained from per-cycle durations, not replaying the serialized reciprocal. Floating-point allowance 1e-12 s for exact synthetic timing.
references.provenance: https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-1/pages/15-1-simple-harmonic-motion# Period and Frequency definitions; independent constructed cycle log

references.method: Published Example 15.1 input period 0.400 microseconds becomes expected 4.00e-7 s; the source output f=2.50e6 Hz is used as local input for this inverse view. Tolerance 5e-10 s is half of the 0.001 microsecond reporting increment. No MHz scale is divided into the expression.

rejection_cases.reason: No finite period exists for zero frequency.

models.inverse_notes: Inverse f=1/T requires T>0 and has one positive root. T=2.5 s gives f=0.4 Hz; substituting yields 1/0.4=2.5 s. T=4e-7 s gives 2.5e6 Hz, matching the published ultrasound example. T=0 is undefined, and f=0 has no finite T. Both zero limits are excluded from this finite-period definition; there are no sign branches.

gaps: Add wave_period and wave_frequency quantity meanings (wave_frequency reused from b01); Hz and s already exist. Oscillator/wave contexts need the same full-cycle semantics; clock_frequency is not an automatic semantic alias.
